app.name: Budget Owl
nav.label: Main
error.generic: Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a moment.
error.network: Budget Owl could not be reached. Check that the server is running and that you are connected, then try again.
error.validation-failed: Some of what you entered is not valid. Check the highlighted fields.
error.malformed-request: That request could not be understood. Reload the page and try again.
error.password-unacceptable.too-short: That password is too short. Use at least {minimumLength} characters.
error.password-unacceptable.too-long: That password is too long. Use at most {maximumBytes} bytes.
error.password-unacceptable.breached: That password appears on a list of commonly used passwords. Choose a different one.
error.password-unacceptable: That password cannot be used. Choose a different one.
error.authentication-failed: The email address or password is not right.
error.not-authenticated: You are not signed in. Sign in and try again.
error.forbidden: You do not have permission to do that.
error.not-a-member: You are not a member of this household.
error.owner-only: Only an owner of the household can do that.
error.read-only-role: Your role in this household is read-only.
error.own-role-unchangeable: Nobody can change their own role. Ask another owner.
error.csrf-token-required: Your session could not be verified. Reload the page and try again.
error.current-password-incorrect: The current password is not right.
error.not-found: That could not be found. It may have been removed.
error.invitation-unusable: This invitation link cannot be used. It may have expired, been used already, or been cancelled. Ask the person who invited you for a new one.
error.setup-already-complete: This instance has already been set up. Sign in instead.
error.invitation-refused: An invitation could not be created for that email address.
error.invitation-requires-sign-out: You are signed in. Sign out before accepting an invitation.
error.last-owner: A household must keep at least one owner. Make someone else an owner first.
error.conflict: That conflicts with a change made elsewhere. Reload the page and try again.
error.stale-version: Somebody else changed this while you were editing it. Nothing has been saved.
error.account-not-empty: This account has transactions recorded against it, so it cannot be deleted. Archive it instead — it keeps its history and disappears from your lists.
error.account-currency-immutable: This account's currency cannot be changed now that it has transactions. The amounts already recorded would mean something different.
error.rate-limited: Too many attempts. Wait {minutes} and try again.
error.internal-error: Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a moment.
validation.lastFour: Enter exactly four digits, or leave this empty.
validation.amount: Enter an amount using digits and a dot, like 1250.00 or -400.
validation.maxBytes: That is too long. Use at most {max} bytes.
validation.server: This value was not accepted. Check it and try again.
setup.title: Set up Budget Owl
setup.lede: This instance is new. Create the first account — it becomes the owner of your household.
setup.operatorNote: You are the person running this instance, so you will be able to see everything anyone in your household records. Anyone you invite is told that before they join.
setup.name: Your name
setup.passwordHint: At least {min} characters. A long phrase is stronger than a clever short one.
setup.baseCurrencyHint: The currency totals are shown in by default. Each member can choose to see another.
login.title: Sign in
login.lede: Welcome back. Sign in to see your household's budget.
login.heading: Your account
login.notice.expired: Your session ended. Sign in again to continue.
login.notice.created: Your account is ready. Sign in to continue.
login.notice.joined: You have joined the household. Sign in to continue.
role.OWNER.description: everything, including inviting and removing people
role.MEMBER.description: can see and change the household's money
role.VIEWER.description: can see the household's money, but not change it
noHousehold.title: You are not part of a household yet
noHousehold.body: You are signed in, but nobody has added you to a household. Ask the person who runs this instance for an invitation link, then open it in this browser.
household.title: Household
household.lede: The household is the shared pot of money everyone here sees. This instance holds one.
household.name: Household name
household.baseCurrencyHint: Totals are shown in this currency unless a member chooses another in their preferences.
household.ownerOnlyEdit: Only an owner can change these.
members.heading: Members
members.removeMessage: {name} will lose access to this household straight away and be signed out everywhere. What they recorded stays in the household.
members.leaveMessage: You will lose access straight away. What you recorded stays in the household, and you will need a new invitation to come back.
members.soleOwner: You are the only owner. Make someone else an owner before you can leave.
invite.title: Invite someone
invite.intro: Create a link and send it to them however you like — a message, or read it out. There is no email.
invite.emailHint: If they are new to this instance, this becomes the address they sign in with — so check it. The link is what lets them in; the address is who they become.
invite.shareIntro: Share this link with {email}. This is the only time it is shown.
invite.copyManual: The link is selected. Copy it with your keyboard.
invite.credentialWarning: Treat this link like a password: anyone who has it can join this household as {role}. It works once and expires {expires}.
invite.linkUnavailable: The link could not be built. Cancel this invitation and create a new one.
invite.revoked: This link has been revoked and can no longer be used.
devices.title: Devices
devices.lede: Every browser and phone where you are signed in. Sign one out and it stops working immediately.
devices.heading: Where you are signed in
devices.revoked: That device has been signed out.
devices.confirmMessage: This is the browser you are using now. You will be signed out and taken to the sign-in screen.
preferences.title: Your preferences
preferences.lede: These are yours alone. They change what you see, never what is recorded, so everyone in the household can read the same figures their own way.
preferences.heading: Display
preferences.currencyHint: Each account keeps its own currency; this is the one totals are shown in for you.
preferences.localeHint: Text appears in this language where a translation exists, and in English otherwise. Dates and numbers always follow your choice.
join.title: Join a household
join.lede: Someone has invited you to share a household's budget on this Budget Owl instance.
join.disclosure.heading: Before you join: who can see your finances
join.disclosure.operator: The person who runs this instance can see everything you record in it: every transaction, every balance, every note.
join.disclosure.nothingHidden: Budget Owl does not hide your data from them, and everyone else in the household can see it too.
join.disclosure.trust: Only join if you are comfortable sharing your finances with the person who runs this server.
join.accountNote: New here? Enter your name and choose a password. Already have an account on this instance? Leave both fields empty and you will be added with it.
join.name: Your name
join.joinedAccountCreated: Your account has been created. Sign in with {email}.
join.signedInBody: An invitation can only be accepted by someone who is signed out. Sign out here, and this page will let you accept it.
accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.lede: Where your household's money sits. Tell Budget Owl about each account once, and transactions can be recorded against the right one.
accounts.heading: Your accounts
accounts.emptyBody: An account is a place money sits — a current account, a savings pot, a credit card, or cash in a tin. Add the ones you have and you can start recording what happens in them.
accounts.emptyReadOnly: Your role in this household is read-only, so someone else will need to add them.
accounts.notShown: {count} more accounts are not shown here.
accounts.notShownOne: 1 more account is not shown here.
accounts.archivedNote: These keep their history and take no new transactions.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.nameHint: Whatever you call it. Two accounts may share a name — the last four digits tell them apart.
accounts.lastFourHint: Optional, and only if it has a number. It is shown beside the name so you can tell two similar accounts apart. Clear this box to remove them.
accounts.currencyHint: The currency this account is held in. Nothing is ever converted behind your back.
accounts.currencyLocked: The currency cannot be changed once an account has transactions: the amounts already recorded would quietly start meaning something else.
accounts.openingBalanceHint: What the account held when you started tracking it. A credit card you owe on starts negative, like -400. Use digits and a dot.
accounts.archiveMessage: It keeps its history, hides it from lists, and stops taking new transactions. Its balance leaves the subtotal for its currency, so that figure will change. You can bring it back whenever you like.
accounts.unarchivedNotice: That account is back in your lists.
accounts.deleteMessage: This permanently removes the account, and it cannot be undone. To keep an account's history, archive it instead.
accounts.conflictBody: Nothing you typed has been saved. This is what the account says now:
accounts.archivedNoteWritable: These keep their history and take no new transactions. Bring one back at any time.
categories.title: Categories
categories.lede: How you group what your money was for. Edit these to match how you actually think about your spending.
categories.heading: Your categories
categories.name: Name
categories.parentHint: Categories can be two levels deep, like Bills then Utilities.
categories.hasChildrenHint: This category has sub-categories, so it can't sit under another one.
categories.kindFixedHint: A category's kind can't change, because that would reinterpret everything already filed under it.
categories.kindFromParentHint: A sub-category uses the same kind as the category it sits under.
categories.emptyBody: Categories let you see where your money goes. You started with a set — if you've deleted them all, add the ones you want.
categories.emptyReadOnly: Ask an owner or member of your household to add some.
categories.archiveMessage: It stops appearing when you record a transaction, and your past transactions still show it. You can restore it at any time.
categories.deleteMessage: Your transactions are kept — they'll just need a category again. This can't be undone.
categories.deleteMessageWithChildren: Its {count} sub-categories are deleted too. Your transactions are kept — they'll just need a category again. This can't be undone.
categories.archivedNote: These don't appear when you record a transaction, but your past transactions still show them.
transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.lede: Everything that's happened to your money. Record what you spend as you go — you can always put a category on it later.
transactions.heading: Your transactions
transactions.accountFixedHint: A transaction stays in the account it was recorded against. To move it, delete it and record it again.
transactions.direction: Which way did the money go?
transactions.amountHint: In {currency}, the currency of the account you chose.
transactions.payeeHint: Optional. Start typing and we'll suggest ones you've used before.
transactions.statusHint: Leave this as Cleared unless you're recording something you expect to settle later.
transactions.deleteMessage: Your account balance goes back to what it was. This can't be undone.
transactions.searchHint: Looks in notes and payee names.
transactions.noMatches: Nothing matches what you're looking for. Try widening the dates, or clearing the filters.
transactions.emptyBody: Nothing recorded yet. Add what you've spent and your account balances will start to mean something.
transactions.emptyReadOnly: Ask an owner or member of your household to record some.
transactions.noAccountsBody: A transaction has to go somewhere, so add an account first.
transactions.mixedCurrencies: No total — this page mixes currencies.
envelopes.title: Envelopes
envelopes.lede: Money you've set aside for the spending that changes week to week. Log what you spend and see what's left, straight away.
envelopes.heading: Your envelopes
envelopes.name: Name
envelopes.nameHint: Keep them narrow — “Groceries” and “Eating out” are two envelopes, not one.
envelopes.monthFixedHint: An envelope stays in the month it was set for. Make a new one for another month.
envelopes.logEmpty: Nothing logged against this envelope yet.
envelopes.emptyBody: An envelope is an amount you decide on and spend down — groceries, eating out, fuel. Set one up and you'll see what's left as you go.
envelopes.emptyReadOnly: Ask an owner or member of your household to set some up.
envelopes.archiveMessage: It stops taking new entries and drops out of this month's list. Everything you've logged against it is kept. You can restore it at any time.
envelopes.deleteMessage: Its {count} logged entries go with it. Your transactions are kept — only the envelope's own record of them is removed. This can't be undone.
envelopes.deleteEntryMessage: The amount goes back to {name}. If it came from a transaction, the transaction itself is kept.
envelopes.archivedNote: These don't take new entries, but what you logged against them is still here.
bills.title: Bills & income
bills.lede: The predictable half of your money: what arrives on a schedule, and what leaves on a date. With your envelopes, that is enough to say what is left.
bills.shortNote: Your income this month does not cover the bills and what you have set aside. Nothing is wrong with the figures — they are telling you something.
bills.heading: Your bills
bills.emptyBody: A bill is something that leaves on a date — rent, a phone contract, a season ticket. Set one up and it is listed before it is due, so nothing surprises you.
bills.emptyReadOnly: Ask an owner or member of your household to set some up.
bills.name: Name
bills.nameHint: What you would call it out loud — “Rent”, “Phone”.
bills.expectedAmountHint: What you expect it to be, in {currency}.
bills.amountVariesHint: For a bill that is never quite the same twice, like electricity.
bills.toleranceHint: How far from the expected amount is unremarkable, in {currency}. A payment further out than that is flagged.
bills.dayOfMonthHint: The 29th, 30th and 31st fall on the last day of a shorter month.
bills.anchorDateHint: A date it was due. “Every other week” needs one, or it names two different sets of days.
bills.irregularHint: An irregular bill has no set date. It is listed here, and you record each payment as it happens.
bills.noneIrregular: No set date, so nothing is due in particular. Record a payment when one happens.
bills.actualAmountHint: What really left the account. The budgeted figure is filled in for you.
bills.dueDateHint: An irregular bill has no date of its own, so this is the date the payment is recorded against.
bills.forgotten: Forgotten. That date reads as planned again.
bills.retireMessage: It stops being listed in new months and keeps every payment you have already recorded. You can restore it at any time.
bills.deleteMessage: Everything recorded about this bill goes with it. Your transactions are kept — a bill is a plan, not a payment. This can't be undone.
bills.forgetMessage: This removes what was recorded for that date, so it reads as planned again. It is not the same as marking it due: that is you saying it is unpaid, and this is saying nothing at all.
bills.retiredNote: These are not listed in new months, and everything recorded against them is kept.
bills.income.heading: Income
bills.income.emptyBody: An income source is money arriving on a schedule — a salary, a pension, a regular payment from a tenant. Add one and this page can say what is left once the predictable things are accounted for.
bills.income.name: Name
bills.income.nameHint: What you would call it out loud — “Salary”, “Pension”.
bills.income.amountHint: What arrives on each date, in {currency}. The month's total is worked out from the schedule.
bills.income.retireMessage: It stops counting towards what is expected in new months. You can restore it at any time.
bills.income.deleteMessage: This income source goes, along with what it contributed to any month's figures. Your transactions are kept. This can't be undone.
bills.envelopes.heading: Envelopes
bills.envelopes.body: The other half of the subtraction: what you have set aside for the spending that changes week to week. Envelopes have a screen of their own.
error.bill-inactive: This bill is retired, so nothing new can be recorded against it. Restore it first — what was already recorded is kept.
error.bill-name-taken: You already have a bill with that name.
error.income-name-taken: You already have an income source with that name.
bills.billsCountEitherWay: Bills count here whether or not you have paid them. Money that has already gone is not money you still have, so ticking one off does not change this figure.
transfers.noCategoryNote: Moving money between two of your own accounts isn't spending and isn't income, so a transfer has no category and nobody to pay.
transfers.editBothHalves: Changes here apply to both halves — what left one account and what arrived in the other stay in step.
transfers.accountsFixedHint: A transfer stays between the two accounts you made it with, so there's nothing to change here. To move it to different accounts, delete it and make it again.
transfers.amountHint: In {currency}, the currency of the account it leaves. No minus sign — which way it went is the two accounts above.
transfers.amountHintNoAccount: Choose the account it leaves and we'll tell you which currency this is in.
transfers.amountReceivedHint: These two accounts are in different currencies, so what arrived isn't the same number as what left — and only your statement knows it. Copy it from there, in {received}.
transfers.impliedRateNote: Worked out by dividing the two figures above, just so you can see it. It isn't the rate your bank gave you — that had its fee inside it — and nothing in Budget Owl uses it.
transfers.noteHint: Optional. Both halves of the transfer get it.
transfers.deleteMessage: Both halves go, and both account balances go back to what they were. This can't be undone.
transactions.transferPairOnly: Both halves of a transfer change together, so this row can't be edited on its own.
validation.positiveAmount: Enter an amount using digits and a dot, like 200 or 49.99. No minus sign.
validation.sameAccount: Choose a different account. Money can't move from an account to itself.
error.account-archived: That account is archived, so nothing new can be recorded against it. Restore it first — what's already recorded is kept.
error.transfer-leg-not-separate: This is one half of a transfer, and the two halves are always changed together. Edit or delete the transfer itself.
admin.title: Administration
admin.lede: Who can sign in to this server, and how. Everything else an operator does — backups, upgrades, the database — is done on the machine, because the machine is yours.
admin.nothingChanged: Nothing had changed, so nothing was saved.
admin.registrationConsequence: While registration is open, anybody who can reach this server over the network can create themselves an account. If it is reachable from the internet, that means anybody at all. Leave it closed and invite the people you want instead.
admin.passwordSwitch: Offer sign-in with an email address and a password
admin.passwordHint: Email and password is a permanent part of Budget Owl. Once another way in is working you can stop offering this one, but it is always in the build and can always be switched back on.
admin.passwordOn: Email and password sign-in is on.
admin.passwordLockedTitle: This cannot be turned off yet
admin.passwordLockedRule: An owner has to complete a sign-in through your provider first. Proving the new way in works before the old one is hidden is what stops you being locked out of your own records, on your own hardware, with nobody to call.
admin.passwordOffRecovery: If your provider later stops working, this is switched back on from the machine itself. On the server, run:
admin.passwordOffRecoveryAfter: Nothing in the browser can help once the browser is the thing you cannot get in through.
admin.oidcLede: Optional. If you already run an identity provider, this adds a second way in. It changes nothing about what anybody may see once they are signed in.
admin.oidcOffWarning: Turning this off also switches email and password sign-in back on, so that nobody is left without a way in.
admin.oidcProven: An owner signed in through your provider on {date}, so email and password sign-in can now be turned off.
admin.oidcNotProven: No owner has signed in through your provider yet. Until one has, email and password sign-in stays on.
admin.oidcIssuerHint: Where your provider publishes its configuration, such as https://id.example.org. Use https: the client secret is sent to this host.
admin.oidcClientIdHint: The identifier your provider issued for Budget Owl.
admin.oidcSecretHint: Budget Owl never shows a stored secret back — not to anybody, including you. Leave this empty to keep the one you have, or type a new one to replace it. If you cannot remember it, replace it.
admin.oidcProvisioning: Create an account for anybody who signs in through the provider
admin.oidcProvisioningHint: An account on its own sees nothing. Joining the household still needs an invitation, so nobody in your provider's directory lands inside your finances.
admin.oidcOffMessage: Email and password sign-in will be switched back on, so that nobody is left without a way in. Your provider's details are cleared, and anybody who signed in through it will need a password instead.
admin.conflictMessage: These settings changed after this page read them, so nothing has been saved and what you entered is still here.
admin.conflictNothingVisible: Nothing visible here changed, but somebody saved these settings while you were editing them.
admin.accountsLede: Everybody who can sign in to this server. Read-only here — suspending or removing an account is not something this screen does.
error.not-instance-admin: Only the person who administers this instance can do that. On a self-hosted Budget Owl that is whoever set it up.
error.password-login-locked: Email and password sign-in cannot be turned off yet. An owner has to complete a sign-in through your provider first, which proves the new way in works before the old one is hidden.
validation.issuerUrl: Enter the provider's address starting with https:// — or http:// only if it runs on this same machine.
debt.title: Debt plan
debt.lede: Your balances, one order of attack. Minimums come from your bills; the extra comes from what is left after your goals.
debt.empty.heading: Nothing owed here yet
debt.empty.body: A debt is a balance you are reducing, with terms. Add one and Budget Owl ranks it against the others, works out when each is gone, and shows you what the two usual orders of attack would cost you.
debt.empty.counted: If a debt's minimum is already a bill, say which bill — it is then counted once, not twice.
debt.emptyReadOnly: You can see the plan, and only an owner or a member can add a debt.
debt.header: {committed} a month committed · {strategic} of it strategic
debt.strategyNote: Changing this changes every date on this page. Both orders are worked out either way, so you can compare before you choose.
debt.mixedCurrency: Your debts are in more than one currency, so there is no single debt-free date and no combined interest total. Each currency is worked out on its own — converting would need a rate this instance may not have.
debt.headline: {owed} to clear · debt-free {month} on this plan
debt.headline.noDate: {owed} to clear · no debt-free date yet, because {reason}
debt.belowMinimums: {amount} a month is less than the {minimums} your debts ask for as minimums.
debt.belowMinimumsNote: There is no order to build from that, so no dates are shown. Nothing here is a judgement — the figures are yours and this page will work the moment the monthly amount covers the minimums.
debt.rationale.AVALANCHE: Highest rate first, so the money goes where it is costing you most.
debt.rationale.SNOWBALL: Smallest balance first, so the first debt is gone soonest — which some people need to keep going.
debt.card.noInterest: No interest total, because this order has no end date yet.
debt.comparison.both: {cheaper} costs less in interest. {sooner} clears your first debt {months} months sooner. Either is a good answer.
debt.comparison.cheaperOnly: {cheaper} costs less in interest, and both clear your first debt in the same month. Either is a good answer.
debt.comparison.same: Both orders cost the same and finish together, so take whichever you will stick to.
debt.whatIf.months: Adding {step} a month would make you debt-free {month} — {months} months sooner.
debt.whatIf.oneMonth: Adding {step} a month would make you debt-free {month} — a month sooner.
debt.whatIf.noChange: Adding {step} a month would not move the date: {month} either way.
debt.openAny: Open any debt for its terms and payments.
debt.tableCaption: Your debts in {strategy} order, with what each one is paying and when it clears.
debt.footer: Minimums · each counted once in Bills & income, so a debt whose minimum is already a bill row is not asked for twice — {minimums}
debt.rateReleased: Terms saved. The rate is now worked out from your other figures and is marked Solved.
debt.balance.estimated: An estimate — {months} months assumed since you last confirmed it
debt.balance.stale: Estimated for over a year. Check a statement — last confirmed {date}.
debt.reason.neverClears: the payment is less than the interest this balance builds up, so it grows
debt.reason.belowMinimums: the monthly amount is less than the minimums
debt.reason.unknown: there is no projection for it
debt.clears.never: Does not clear — the payment is under the interest
debt.clears.noPlan: No date — the monthly amount is under the minimums
debt.paying.minimumUntil: Minimum {amount} a month until the rung above clears
debt.paying.clearsIt: {amount} — all that is left to clear it
debt.field.name: What you call it
debt.field.nameHint: Whatever you would say out loud — “Visa”, “Car loan”.
debt.field.kindHint: A card revolves; an installment loan has a term.
debt.field.servicerHint: Optional. The lender or servicer on the statement.
debt.field.balanceHint: In {currency}, digits and a dot — like 6180.00.
debt.field.balanceDate: The date that balance was true
debt.field.balanceDateHint: Off the statement. The balance and its date travel together, so that later figures can say where they came from.
debt.field.aprHint: The percentage the statement prints — like 22.9. Zero is a real promotional rate and is accepted.
debt.field.aprSolved: Work the rate out for me
debt.field.aprSolvedHint: Hands the rate back to Budget Owl, which works it out from your other figures and marks it Solved. Your own figure is removed.
debt.field.aprAlreadySolved: This rate is already worked out from your other figures. Untick to enter one of your own.
debt.field.minimumHint: What the lender asks for each month. It never changes this debt's own forecast — it is the floor your plan allocates.
debt.field.originalBalanceHint: Optional, and only used to show progress. Left blank, no progress figure is shown rather than a misleading 0%.
debt.field.accountHint: Optional. A debt you track by hand is ordinary — nothing here needs a bank.
debt.field.currencyHint: Totals are worked out per currency, never converted.
debt.field.bill: The bill that pays its minimum
debt.field.billHint: Say which bill and the minimum is counted once. Budget Owl never guesses this from a name or an amount — the figure it decides is what you have left this month.
bills.owed.heading: Owed
bills.owed.body: What you owe in all. This is a balance, not a monthly commitment, so it is not taken off what is left — doing that would tell a household owing a year's wages that it has nothing to spend this month.
bills.owed.notInBills: {amount} of those minimums is not already a bill row this month, and that is the part taken off what is left. The rest is already counted in your bills.
bills.owed.mixedCurrency: The count covers debts in every currency; the two totals are {currency} only. They do not describe the same set of debts, because adding currencies together would need a rate this instance may not have.
bills.owed.none: No debts recorded, so nothing here comes off what is left.
bills.owed.asOfToday: These two totals and the count are as they stand today, not as they stood in the month shown — a balance as at a past month would need a day-by-day ledger Budget Owl does not keep.
debt.chart.coincide: One line here stands for all of these orders: {lines}. Over this plan they stay closer together than the chart can draw. The cards below give each one's own figures.
debt.monthlyAmountHint: What you put against your debts in all, minimums included. Every date on this page is worked out from it.
debt.terms.heading: Loan terms
debt.terms.promise: Give me any three of the rate, the payment and the horizon and I will work out the fourth. Anything marked Solved is my arithmetic, not your word.
debt.terms.balanceNeverSolved: The balance is never worked out from the other figures. It is the one number you can read off a statement, so it only ever changes when you say so.
debt.balance.staleLabel: last confirmed over a year ago
debt.balance.estimatedLine: An estimate: {months} months rolled forward from the {amount} you confirmed on {date}, assuming the minimum was paid and the interest in between was added.
debt.balance.staleLine: Estimated for over a year, so this is the {amount} you confirmed on {date} rather than a year of guesses. A statement figure would put it right.
debt.chart.detailAssumes: The first line assumes {amount} a month.
debt.chart.buying: Paying {extra} extra is buying you {months} months: gone by {soon} instead of {late}.
debt.chart.atMinimumNote: The comparison line assumes the minimum never changes. A card's real minimum falls as the balance falls, which stretches it out further still — so the comparison is kinder to the minimum than reality is.
debt.history.heading: Payment history
debt.history.empty: Nothing recorded against this one yet. The balance is the figure you confirmed, carried forward.
debt.history.caption: Every payment recorded against {name}, with how each row got here.
debt.history.showAll: Showing the most recent {count}. The rest are a page away.
debt.history.compounding: Interest is the balance times the annual rate, divided by twelve, until a statement says otherwise — then the statement wins and the gap is recorded as a correction. It is a simplification you can check with a calculator, and it is not what your lender will charge to the penny.
debt.payment.title: Log a payment to {name}
debt.payment.lede: Filled in with what your plan puts against this one. Change the amount if you paid something else.
debt.payment.paidFromHint: Which of your accounts the money left. Nothing is recorded against that account and no transaction is created — this is only where a matching charge will be looked for later.
debt.payment.splitNote: Budget Owl works out how much of this went on interest and how much came off the balance, using the rate in force on the day, and shows you both the moment it is recorded.
debt.payment.recorded: Payment recorded: {interest} interest · {principal} principal. Balance now {balance}.
debt.balanceConfirmed: Balance confirmed. Anything the arithmetic had wrong is recorded as a correction rather than tidied away.
debt.estimate.title: Is this still right?
debt.estimate.assumed: That is an estimate. I have assumed {months} months of {minimum} payments since you last confirmed it, and added the interest in between.
debt.estimate.staleBody: It has been {months} months with nothing confirmed, so rather than carry a year of guesses forward this shows the {amount} you last told me.
debt.estimate.correctionNote: If your figure disagrees with my arithmetic, the difference is recorded as a correction in the history. Nothing already recorded is quietly changed.
debt.estimate.stopEstimating: Stop estimating — use the last figure I confirmed
debt.chart.noLine: There is no line to draw, because {reason}.
debt.estimate.figureEstimate: my estimate of what is owed now
debt.arrangeHint: Move a debt up or down to set the order yourself; the dates are worked out again each time.
debt.payment.carriesMonthInterest: This includes {month}'s interest of {interest}. Interest is charged once a month, on the first payment dated in that month — any further payment in {month} comes off the balance in full.
debt.payment.monthInterestAlreadyCharged: No interest on this one: {month}'s interest was charged on an earlier payment, so all of it comes off the balance.
debt.payment.previewUnavailable: I could not work out the split just now. You can still record the payment — the interest and the principal will be shown on it once it is.
debt.tableCaptionCustom: Your debts in the order you chose, with what each one is paying and when it clears.
debt.yourOrder: Your own order: debt-free {month}, with {amount} of interest along the way.
debt.yourOrder.noDate: Your own order has no debt-free date, because {reason}.
error.report-range-invalid: That range of months doesn't work. Choose a start month on or before the end month.
error.report-range-too-long: Insights can show at most {maximumMonths} months at a time.
insights.title: Insights
insights.lede: What actually happened in your ledger, month by month. Every figure is added up from your transactions each time you open this page.
insights.currency.label: Currency
insights.currency.note: Each currency is reported on its own, with no combined figure: adding them together would need an exchange rate.
insights.range.label: Range
insights.range.12.name: Last 12 months
insights.range.6.name: Last 6 months
insights.range.3.name: Last 3 months
insights.income.heading: Income vs spending
insights.keptLong: Kept an average of {amount} a month. Best month was {month}, at {best}.
insights.keptLongPartial: Kept an average of {amount} a month over the {count} complete months. Best month was {month}, at {best}.
insights.keptLongPartialOne: Kept {amount} in the one complete month so far, {month}.
insights.chart.label: Income and spending by month
insights.coincident: Income and spending were the same every month, so they are drawn as one line.
insights.chart.negative: A month where refunds were more than spending is drawn at zero. The table shows its real figure.
insights.uncategorised.one.single: 1 transaction needs a category, so {amount} isn't counted as income or spending.
insights.uncategorised.many.single: {count} transactions need a category, so {amount} isn't counted as income or spending.
insights.uncategorised.one.both: 1 transaction needs a category, so {out} out and {in} in aren't counted as income or spending.
insights.uncategorised.many.both: {count} transactions need a category, so {out} out and {in} in aren't counted as income or spending.
insights.downloadIncome: of income and spending by month
insights.figures.caption: Income and spending by month, {range}, in {currency}.
insights.envelopes: Insights counts the transactions in your ledger. Amounts logged straight into an envelope don't appear here.
insights.where.heading: Where {month} went
insights.where.uncategorised.one: Needs a category: {amount} across 1 transaction, not in the list above.
insights.where.uncategorised.many: Needs a category: {amount} across {count} transactions, not in the list above.
goals.title: Goals
goals.lede: Money you are putting aside for something. What you plan to set aside each month comes off what's left to spend.
goals.empty.heading: Nothing you are saving for yet
goals.empty.body: A goal is money you put aside for something — an emergency fund, a trip, a deposit. Give it a name and how much it needs, with a month if you have one, and see it fill up.
goals.emptyReadOnly: Your role is read-only, so goals are added by an owner or a member.
goals.countsTowardsLeft: Each goal's monthly amount is taken off what's left to spend this month, on Bills & income. It counts in full whether or not you have set it aside yet.
goals.archived.heading: Archived goals
goals.archived.body: An archived goal keeps its history but is no longer part of the month's plan, so nothing it planned or recorded comes off what's left to spend.
goals.reason.beyondHorizon: At {monthly} a month it is more than fifty years away.
goals.reason.targetMonthPassed: The month you picked has passed.
goals.reason.notReachable: This month started with the goal reached, so this month's plan no longer counts. Record the rest directly to make {target}.
goals.required.noContribution: Set a monthly amount to see when you get there.
goals.required.beyondHorizon: The month you picked is more than fifty years away, so there is no monthly figure for it.
goals.required.noTargetMonth: There is no target month, so there is no monthly figure to aim for.
goals.required.targetMonthPassed: The month you picked has passed, so there is no monthly figure to reach it by then.
goals.projection.reaches: At {monthly} a month you reach it in {month}.
goals.projection.onTime: At {monthly} a month you reach it in {month}, in time for {target}.
goals.projection.lateOne: At {monthly} a month you reach it in {month} — 1 month after {target}.
goals.projection.late: At {monthly} a month you reach it in {month} — {count} months after {target}.
goals.projection.overdueReaches: Overdue since {target} — at {monthly} a month you reach it in {month}.
goals.projection.required: {amount} a month gets you there by {target}.
goals.projection.planReaches: Keeping to its plan, you reach it in {month}.
goals.projection.planOnTime: Keeping to its plan, you reach it in {month}, in time for {target}.
goals.projection.planLateOne: Keeping to its plan, you reach it in {month} — 1 month after {target}.
goals.projection.planLate: Keeping to its plan, you reach it in {month} — {count} months after {target}.
goals.projection.planOverdueReaches: Overdue since {target} — keeping to its plan, you reach it in {month}.
goals.previewUnavailable: The figures could not be worked out just now. You can still save.
goals.noInterest: This assumes no interest or growth: a goal is what you put in.
goals.field.name: What it is for
goals.field.monthHint: Leave it empty for a goal with no date, like an emergency fund.
goals.field.alreadySavedHint: Money you had already put by before you started tracking it. It counts towards the goal and never towards any month's left-over figure.
goals.field.monthlyHint: What you plan to set aside every month, from this month. It comes off what's left to spend.
goals.field.accountHint: For your reference. The goal's figure comes from what you record here, because one account often holds several goals.
goals.field.currencyHint: Fixed once the goal is added. A goal kept in an account is in that account's currency.
goals.plan.title: Change the plan for {name}
goals.plan.thisMonthUnchanged: {month} stays as it is. The new amount applies from the month after.
goals.contribute.prefilled: Filled in with what is still to come for {month}: {amount}. Change it for a top-up.
goals.contribute.noLedger: This records it against the goal only. Nothing is added to or taken from any account — move the money at your bank as usual.
goals.detail.over: Reached, with {amount} more than the target.
goals.detail.accountBalance: {account} has {amount}. That is the account's balance, not this goal's.
goals.detail.alreadySaved: Already saved when you started tracking it: {amount}
goals.detail.historyCaption: Money set aside for this goal and taken out of it, newest first.
goals.unarchived: The goal is restored, and is part of the month's plan again.
goals.archive.heading: Archive {name}?
goals.archive.body: Its history stays, and it stops being part of the month's plan. Anything it planned or recorded this month stops coming off what's left to spend, so that figure goes up.
goals.delete.heading: Delete {name} permanently?
goals.delete.body: This deletes the goal, its plan and everything recorded against it, permanently. No transaction is touched. To keep the history, archive it instead.
goals.removeContribution.heading: Remove this from {name}?
goals.removeContribution.body: The goal's figure changes to match. Nothing in any account is touched.
error.goal-limit-reached: This household has as many goals, or this goal as many records, as one household can hold. Archive or delete one first.
error.goal-name-taken: You already have a goal with this name. Choose a different one.
error.goal-archived: This goal is archived. Restore it to set money aside or change its plan.
error.goal-plan-period-past: The plan can only change from this month on. To correct a past month, record or remove what was set aside then.
error.goal-plan-period-too-far: The plan can only change up to two years ahead. Choose an earlier month.
error.goal-currency-mismatch: That account is in a different currency from this goal, so it cannot hold it.
bills.goalsNote: Goals count what you plan to set aside each month, or what you recorded if that is more. Money already saved before you started tracking a goal is never counted.
bills.debtExtraExceedsLeft: Your debt plan puts {extra} a month towards debt beyond the minimums, which is more than the {left} left this month after your goals. Nothing has been changed — adjust the plan or a goal if you need to.
debt.extraExceedsLeft: This plan's extra of {extra} a month is more than the {left} left this month after your bills, envelopes and goals. Nothing changes automatically.
transfers.legDates: The two halves are dated {from} and {to}. A date saved here moves both to it; leave it as it is and each keeps its own.
transfers.legNotes: The two halves have different notes. A note saved here replaces both; leave it as it is and each keeps its own.
pairing.title: Pair this with the other half of a transfer
pairing.intro: Choose the row in your other account that this money moved to or from. Nothing is chosen for you.
pairing.none: No rows match. Try another account or other dates.
pairing.loss: Both rows will lose their category and payee, and stop counting as income or spending. Splitting them later brings back two rows with no category.
pairing.splitHeading: Split this transfer into two rows?
pairing.splitMessage: Both rows stay, with their amounts and dates, but come back with no category and no payee, so they'll be in Needs a category. They'll count as income and spending again.
pairing.splitDone: Split into two rows. Both need a category.
import.title: Import a statement
import.lede: Bring in transactions from a file your bank exported. You'll see exactly what will be added before anything is.
import.viewerBody: Your role in this household is read-only. An owner or a member can import a statement for you.
import.noAccountsBody: An import needs an account to put the transactions in. Add one first.
import.stepFile: The file, and where it goes
import.fileHint: OFX, QFX, QIF or CSV, up to 5 MB. It is read by your own Budget Owl server and isn't kept after the import.
import.dropHint: Or drop the file onto this box.
import.balanceAfterWithSuspected: If you include every one that looks typed
import.outOfDate: You have changed how the file is read. Update the preview to see what that does before you import.
import.formatHint: Picked from the file's name. Change it if that's wrong; the file is checked either way.
import.tooLarge: That file is larger than 5 MB, the most Budget Owl reads at once. Export a shorter date range from your bank and import it in parts.
import.readFailed: Your browser couldn't open that file. Try choosing it again.
import.nothingWritten: Nothing is added until you confirm.
import.charsetHint: The file doesn't say which character set it uses. Choose the one where names and accents read correctly.
import.charsetAuto: Work it out from the file
import.dateFormatHint: Choose how your bank writes dates.
import.dateFormatAmbiguous: The dates in this file can be read more than one way. Choose how your bank writes them.
import.mappingSuggested: Budget Owl guessed these settings from the file. Check them, then update the preview.
import.mappingSaved: These are the settings you saved for this account.
import.mappingChanged: This file's columns aren't the same as the last file you imported into this account. Check the settings before you update the preview.
import.headerRowHint: Which line holds the column names. 0 if the file has none.
import.moneyOutColumnsHint: Mark the columns below as Money out and Money in, or as In or out.
import.columnsCaption: The first rows of your file, with what each column holds
import.saveMapping: Remember these settings for this account
import.saveMappingHint: Saved when you import, so the next file from this bank needs no setting up.
import.bankSays: Your bank says the balance is {bank}. After this import, Budget Owl will say {after}.
import.balanceDiffers: Those two differ. That's usual when your opening balance or older transactions in Budget Owl don't match the bank's. Worth checking before you rely on either.
import.accountDiffers: This file looks like it belongs to a different account from {account}. Check you chose the right one before importing.
import.suspectedIntro: These look like transactions somebody already typed in, so they're left out unless you tick them.
import.resembles: Looks like the one already in your ledger on {date}.
import.duplicatesIntro: Already in your ledger from an earlier import, so they're skipped.
import.unreadableIntro: These lines couldn't be read and won't be imported. Fix them in the file and import it again if you need them.
import.row.row-date-ambiguous: The date can be read more than one way.
import.row.row-date-out-of-range: The date is too far in the past or the future.
import.row.row-amount-too-precise: The amount has more than four decimal places.
import.row.row-amount-too-large: The amount is larger than Budget Owl records.
import.row.row-currency-mismatch: It's in a different currency from the account.
import.row.row-missing-field: It's missing a date or an amount.
import.row.row-columns-short: It has fewer columns than the rows around it.
import.row.row-entity-unknown: It contains a character code Budget Owl doesn't recognise.
import.attentionTruncated: There are more than are shown here. The counts above include all of them.
import.identicalIntro: These rows are exactly alike, which is normal (two coffees on one day). Each one is imported.
import.reusedIdentifier: Your bank's file used the same reference for more than one transaction, so Budget Owl told them apart by date, amount and payee instead.
import.textCut: Some payees or notes were longer than Budget Owl keeps, so they've been shortened.
import.sample: The first rows to be added
import.nothingNew: There's nothing new to add from this file.
import.stale: Your ledger changed since this preview, so nothing was imported. This is the preview again, with what's there now.
import.staleDuplicates: {count} of these were added by somebody else a moment ago.
import.doneDetail: They're in Needs a category, ready for you to sort.
import.undoMessage: This removes the {count} transactions this import added to {account}. Any of them since linked to a bill, a debt payment or an envelope lose that link. Rows you have paired into a transfer stay.
import.historyCounts: {imported} added · {duplicate} already there · {excluded} left out · {unreadable} unreadable
error.import-file-too-large: That file is larger than Budget Owl reads at once (5 MB). Export a shorter date range and import it in parts. If the file is smaller than that, the server in front of Budget Owl has a lower limit; ask whoever runs it.
error.import-content-encoding-refused: That upload was compressed on the way, which Budget Owl doesn't accept. Reload the page and try again.
error.import-file-malformed: That file can't be read as a bank statement.
error.import-file-malformed.dtd: That file contains a document type declaration. Bank statements don't need one, and Budget Owl doesn't read them.
error.import-file-malformed.binary: That file isn't text. Check you chose the statement your bank exported, not a spreadsheet or a PDF.
error.import-file-malformed.header: The start of that file isn't a valid OFX header.
error.import-file-malformed.line-too-lon: One line in that file is far longer than a statement's.
error.import-file-malformed.too-many-col: That file has more columns than any statement Budget Owl reads.
error.import-file-malformed.too-deep: That file is nested more deeply than any bank statement.
error.import-file-malformed.too-many-ele: That file has more parts than any statement Budget Owl reads.
error.import-file-malformed.element-too-: One value in that file is far longer than a statement's.
error.import-file-malformed.encrypted: That file is password-protected. Export it again without a password.
error.import-file-malformed.compressed: That file is compressed. Unzip it and choose the statement inside.
error.import-file-malformed.not-a-statem: That file doesn't contain a statement Budget Owl can read.
error.import-file-malformed.unclosed-quo: That file has a quote that's never closed, so its columns can't be read.
error.import-format-mismatch: That file isn't in the format you chose. Check the Format setting.
error.import-encoding-unsupported: Budget Owl can't read that character set. Choose another one.
error.import-multiple-accounts: That file holds statements for more than one account. Export one account at a time.
error.import-currency-mismatch: That statement is in a different currency from the account you chose.
error.import-too-many-rows: That file has more than 10,000 transactions, the most Budget Owl reads at once. Export a shorter date range and import it in parts.
error.import-file-too-complex: That file took too long to read. Export a shorter date range and try again.
error.import-preview-stale: Your ledger changed since the preview, so nothing was imported. Preview the file again.
error.transfer-pair-mismatch: Those two rows can't be one transfer.
error.transfer-leg-in-envelope: One of these rows is logged against an envelope. Moving money between your own accounts isn't spending, so take it out of the envelope first, then pair the rows.
error.transfer-pair-mismatch.same-accoun: Both rows are in the same account. A transfer moves money between two different accounts.
error.transfer-pair-mismatch.same-sign: Both rows went the same way. A transfer needs money leaving one account and arriving in the other.
error.transfer-pair-mismatch.amounts-dif: The two amounts aren't equal. In one currency, what left one account has to be what arrived in the other.
checkIn.title: Check-in for week {week}
checkIn.keptAsYouGo: Your answers are kept as you go, on any device. Nothing changes in your budget until you finish.
checkIn.notStartedBody: This is how the week looks so far. Start the check-in to answer it.
checkIn.notStartedReadOnly: Nobody has started this week's check-in yet. You can read it, but only an owner or a member can answer it.
checkIn.readOnly: You can read this check-in. Only an owner or a member can answer it.
checkIn.whatsNew.heading: {count} things to look at
checkIn.whatsNew.quiet: Quiet week otherwise. Nothing else looks out of the ordinary.
checkIn.income.heading: Paycheck landed
checkIn.income.expected: Your plan expects {amount}. Nothing to do.
checkIn.income.notYet: {name}: expected {date}, not seen yet. Nothing to do.
checkIn.odd.heading: Bigger than usual
checkIn.odd.prepaid: {multiple} times the {bill} bill at once? Treat it as prepaid and skip the next {skips}.
checkIn.odd.prepaidOne: {multiple} times the {bill} bill at once? Treat it as prepaid and skip the next one.
checkIn.odd.noOffer: Budget Owl can't tell which bill this is, so there's nothing to record. It's here so you notice it.
checkIn.overdue.heading: Not marked paid
checkIn.overdue.reason: {bill} was due {date} ({amount}) and hasn't been marked paid.
checkIn.categorize.heading: {count} charges need a category
checkIn.categorize.replacesRule: Replaces your rule filing it under {category}.
checkIn.bills.heading: Bills this month
checkIn.charge.outside: Charged {amount}. Your {bill} bill is {expected}. Attach it?
checkIn.charge.recurring: A repeating {amount} has hit {account} three months running. Map it to your {bill} bill?
checkIn.charge.recurringPick: A repeating {amount} has hit {account} three months running. Which bill is it?
checkIn.charge.remember: Remember: this payee in this account pays this bill
checkIn.next.target: This week's target was {target}, and {spent} of unplanned spending went out.
checkIn.next.noTarget: This is your first check-in, so there was no target to measure this week against.
checkIn.next.short: The month is already short, even though this week came in under, so the only place for it is next week.
checkIn.next.negative: That's below zero: this month's plan has already spent more than it has.
checkIn.next.dueNextWeek: That's after {bills}, which it already counts.
checkIn.next.streak: {count} weeks under target in a row.
checkIn.next.streakMoved: {count} weeks under target in a row — that's what moved the debt-free date from {from} to {to}.
checkIn.choice.debtNoDate: {debt} has no payoff month to move yet.
checkIn.choice.debtCarriesInterest: It would be {debt}'s first payment this month, so it carries this month's interest of {interest}. Your regular payment later this month then comes off the balance in full.
checkIn.choice.debtNeverMoves: Records a {amount} payment to {debt} today. Make the payment at your bank — Budget Owl never moves money.
checkIn.choice.goalNeverMoves: Records {amount} set aside for {goal} today. Move the money yourself — Budget Owl never moves money.
checkIn.discardMessage: Every answer in it is deleted. Nothing else changes, because nothing was recorded yet.
checkIn.draftOpen: There's an unfinished check-in for {week}. Finish it or discard it before starting this one.
checkIn.answerConflict: Someone else answered this first. Their answer is shown below.
checkIn.staleIntro: Something changed while you were answering, so nothing was recorded. The marked items need another look.
checkIn.stale.subject-changed: This changed in the ledger after you answered. Check it and answer again.
checkIn.stale.subject-gone: This is no longer part of the week.
checkIn.stale.target-archived: The category you chose has been archived. Choose another.
checkIn.stale.already-recorded: This was recorded on Bills & income in the meantime.
checkIn.stale.transaction-attached-elsew: This charge is now attached to something else.
checkIn.stale.limit-reached: That goal or debt has as many records as it can hold.
checkIn.stale.surplus-changed: This week's surplus changed. Choose again.
checkIn.stale.basis-changed: The week changed while you were answering: new rows, a rule, a bill or a goal. Look it over and finish again.
checkIn.completedLede: Here's what it recorded. Each record lives where it always does, and is corrected there.
checkIn.summary.attachedRemembered: Marked {bill} paid and remembered the mapping.
checkIn.otherCurrencies: {count} transactions this week are in accounts in another currency. A check-in looks only at your base currency.
checkIn.prompt.label: Weekly check-in
checkIn.prompt.quiet: A few minutes to see where the week went.
checkIn.rules.payeeBody: A weekly check-in remembers a payee when you tick "Always file this payee here". A rule only suggests: the next check-in arrives with that row already answered, and you can change it.
checkIn.rules.archived: Archived: suggests nothing until you restore the category.
checkIn.rules.more: {count} more rules are not shown here.
checkIn.mapping.label: Mapped
checkIn.mapping.removed: The mapping was removed. The next check-in will ask about that charge again.
error.check-in-week-out-of-range: That week is too far back or too far ahead for a check-in.
error.check-in-draft-open: There's already an unfinished check-in for another week. Finish or discard it first.
error.check-in-completed: This check-in is already done. A finished check-in can't be changed.
error.check-in-stale: Something changed while you were answering, so nothing was recorded. Look the week over and finish again.
error.check-in-incomplete: Choose where this week's surplus goes before you finish.
error.payee-rule-limit-reached: This household has as many payee rules as it can hold. Remove one on the categories page first.
error.charge-rule-limit-reached: This household has as many bill mappings as it can hold. Unmap one on Bills & income first.
